dedupe_keys.name: semi automated building footprint and occupancy workflow for flood exposure kerala india

description: A semi-automated workflow, published in Natural Hazards in September 2022, for building a database of buildings at risk in places with little data. A deep learning model detects building footprints in a city in Kerala, India, with an F1 score above 76%; the footprints are then classified into 13 occupancy types using morphological metrics and open-source auxiliary data, and given attributes such as average number of floors, total floor space, building density and built-up percentage. Applied to a second Kerala city, the approach gave a similar F1 score of 74%. The authors, Kushanav Bhuyan, Cees van Westen, Jiong Wang and Sansar Raj Meena, also overlaid the buildings on the 2018 flood susceptibility map to find exposed buildings and occupancies. Access: the article is open access under CC BY (Crossref record and article page); no code or data link was found in the record read. Caveats: the authors note the need for a local expert and good auxiliary data to get reasonable occupancy information. Useful for rapid exposure and risk assessment, disaster risk reduction and policy in data-scarce regions; related records are not yet linked.
